transcript.text: My fridge freezer has been making a funny smell in the kitchen the last couple of days, I've cleaned it out but it's still there. Any ideas?

A fridge/freezer smell that remains after cleaning is often coming from somewhere you can’t easily see rather than the food compartment itself.

### First: identify the type of smell
• Burning plastic, hot rubber, “fishy” electrical smell, or smoke: switch it off/unplug it if safe to do so, keep it off, and arrange an appliance engineer. A failing relay, wiring or compressor can smell this way.
• Strong chemical/solvent smell, hissing, or a smell like gas: ventilate the room and avoid flames, smoking, or switching electrical items on/off nearby. Modern fridge refrigerants are usually odourless, but some are flammable, so have it checked professionally.
• Rotten food / drains / mould smell: most commonly a blocked drain, dirty drip tray, spill under a seal, or something behind/beneath the appliance.
• Dead-animal smell: check behind the fridge and around the compressor area; occasionally a mouse can get trapped there.

### Things to check
1. Pull the fridge out and inspect underneath and behind it
   Unplug it first. Look for old food, liquid, dust, pet hair, or anything trapped around the compressor. Vacuum the coils/vent area gently if accessible.

2. Check the condensate/drip tray
   Many fridge freezers have a shallow tray at the back, above or near the compressor, where defrost water evaporates. It can become slimy or smell unpleasant. Clean it with warm soapy water if it is removable and accessible. Don’t force parts or tip water into electrical areas.

3. Clear the internal drain hole
   In many fridge compartments there is a small drain hole at the back, often beneath the salad drawers. If blocked, stagnant water and mould can smell. Use warm water and a soft pipe cleaner/cotton bud or the supplied cleaning tool — not a sharp object.

4. Clean door seals and hidden edges
   Wipe inside the rubber seals, around shelf supports, beneath drawers, and the underside of removable shelves. A small spill in one of these places can persist.

5. Look for standing water or ice
   Water under the vegetable drawers, water leaking onto the floor, or excessive ice can point to a blocked defrost drain or door-seal problem.

6. Check nearby sources
   Sometimes the fridge is only circulating a smell from a bin, drain, dishwasher, or something dropped behind kitchen units.

### Cleaning option
For food/mould odours, use warm soapy water first, then wipe with a mild bicarbonate-of-soda solution (about 1 tablespoon per litre of warm water). Dry thoroughly. Leave an open bowl of bicarbonate of soda or activated charcoal inside afterwards to absorb residual odour.

### Call for repair sooner rather than later if
• the smell is electrical, burning, chemical, or worsening;
• the back of the fridge is unusually hot;
• it is clicking repeatedly, running constantly, or not holding temperature;
• there is oily residue, unexplained leaking, or a hissing sound.

Keep chilled food at 5°C or below and frozen food at -18°C or below while investigating.

Thank you. I'd say it smells like hot plastic, a bit like an electrical burning smell, and it's stronger round the back than inside the fridge. The plug feels a little warm too, and there's been a buzzing noise from the back now and then. Should I unplug it?

Yes — unplug it now if it is safe to do so. A hot-plastic/electrical burning smell, warmth at the plug, and buzzing from the back could indicate a failing plug/socket, compressor relay, wiring fault, or overheating component.

• Do not keep using or re-plugging it to “see if it stops.”
• If the plug, cable, or socket looks melted, discoloured, is very hot, is sparking, or you see smoke: do not touch it. Turn off the circuit at your consumer unit/breaker if you can do so safely, leave the area, and call emergency services if there is smoke or fire.
• Keep flammable items away from it and ventilate the kitchen.
• Arrange an appliance engineer to inspect the fridge freezer, and an electrician if the socket or plug itself seems damaged or overheated. Don’t use that socket for another high-power appliance until it has been checked.

To protect food once unplugged: keep both doors shut. Refrigerated food is generally safest for about 4 hours in a closed fridge; a full freezer can hold temperature for around 48 hours (about 24 hours if half-full). If you have a cooler with ice packs, move high-risk chilled foods such as meat, fish, dairy and cooked leftovers first.
